questions.q: Acetophenone, C₆H₅COCH₃, is treated with mCPBA in CH₂Cl₂. The product is:
questions.explain: Phenyl has a higher migratory aptitude than methyl, so oxygen is inserted between the carbonyl carbon and the ring, giving CH₃COOC₆H₅. Methyl benzoate would need methyl to migrate.

questions.q: The correct order of migratory aptitude in the Baeyer–Villiger oxidation is:
options: Methyl > primary alkyl > phenyl > cyclohexyl > tertiary alkyl
Tertiary alkyl > cyclohexyl > phenyl > primary alkyl > methyl
Phenyl > tertiary alkyl > cyclohexyl > methyl > primary alkyl
Tertiary alkyl > phenyl > primary alkyl > cyclohexyl > methyl
questions.explain: The group that better stabilises positive charge during the concerted shift to oxygen migrates: tertiary > cyclohexyl (secondary) > phenyl > primary > methyl.

questions.q: 3-Methylbutan-2-one is oxidised with a peroxyacid. The ester formed is:
questions.explain: Isopropyl (secondary) outranks methyl, so it moves to oxygen and becomes the alkoxy part: CH₃COOCH(CH₃)₂. Methyl 2-methylpropanoate is what methyl migration would give.

questions.q: 2-Methylcyclohexanone is treated with mCPBA. The major product is:
options: 7-Methyloxepan-2-one (methyl on the carbon bonded to the ring oxygen)
3-Methyloxepan-2-one (methyl on the carbon next to C=O)
questions.explain: The ring CH(CH₃) carbon (secondary) outranks the ring CH₂ carbon (primary), so oxygen is inserted on the substituted side and the ring grows from six to seven atoms. The six-membered lactone would need a ring contraction, which does not happen.
